en: Taal Volcano features a crater lake holding Volcano Island, creating a rare volcano inside a lake inside a volcano setup.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly out into the sea.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, towering at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Lake Mainit is the deepest lake in the Philippines, and its name translates to hot lake because of nearby geothermal springs.
Baguio City sits at a high elevation in the Cordillera mountains, giving it a much cooler climate than lowland areas.
The Philippine archipelago consists of 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of these islands are actually inhabited by people.
Maria Cristina Falls in Mindanao is a dramatic double waterfall that generates massive hydroelectric power for the entire region.
The island of Palawan is home to the Philippine mouse-deer, which is one of the smallest hoofed mammals worldwide.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains entirely by hand over 2,000 years ago by indigenous farmers.
The Philippine Fault Zone is a massive tectonic fracture that stretches over 1,200 kilometers across the length of the archipelago.
